Case: Reginald is a 44-year-old who presents with 2 months of low-back and leg pain. The pain started after a day of heavy yard work and has progressed gradually over time. At present time he is most concerned about the increasing severity of pain, which is affecting his ability to function. When you examine Reginald, you confirm that he has a left foot drop with diminished sensation in the sole of his foot. You order an MRI, which reveals an L5-S1 disc herniation with associated canal stenosis and left neuroforaminal stenosis.

{"pain_severity": 8,
  "offer": "yes",
  "dose": "low",
  "explanation": "A limited opioid prescription may be appropriate as a bridge to definitive treatment for severe radicular pain with neurological deficits."}
